scope: open anchors t28, t75, t90, t248, t275, t518, t538 and the two provisional Turning Points anchors (t75 Ewell, t326 Night Assault)
time_standard: Gettysburg local mean time (LMT), the standard of data-src/time/time_anchors.json. 1863 had no standard time; the reports use unsynchronised army/watch time. Washington (Naval Observatory) time differs from Gettysburg LMT by about 0.8 minute (my arithmetic from longitudes, not a sourced figure), so no offset is applied; the real error is watch error, which the reports themselves show to be 30 to 60 minutes between two witnesses of one event.
sunset_note: Sunset 19:32, civil dusk 20:04, nautical dusk 20:46 LMT on 1 to 3 July 1863 (NOAA algorithm as recorded in time_anchors.json; not checked against an almanac).

method.corpus: historian-src/corpus/or27 and historian-src/raw/or27/passages.jsonl (Internet Archive OCR of the 1889 GPO volumes, original not the 1971 reprint). Page = the corpus folio of the leaf the passage stands on.
method.quote_check: Every quotation was checked twice by script (tmp/clock-hist-a/build.py): (1) as a substring of the repo corpus passage text; (2) as a substring of an independent fresh fetch of the Internet Archive OCR text of the same volume (letters and digits only, case-folded). Quotes are OCR text, so they carry OCR damage. NO page image was opened: a quote that matches the OCR may still differ from the printed page.
method.externals: Internet Archive full texts fetched read-only with an identifying User-Agent, one request per second: Southern Historical Society Papers issues (vol. 4 Dec 1877; vol. 6 Sept and Oct 1878; vol. 26 1898), Battles and Leaders vol. 3, Maine at Gettysburg (1898), Report of the Joint Committee on the Conduct of the War (1865) vol. 1. HathiTrust, Perseus and ehistory.osu.edu were not touched.
method.types: A1 primary report or dispatch of 1863 (or sworn testimony of 1864); A2 memoir written years later; B secondary. Pages for A2/B items come from OCR running heads and are marked 'about' where estimated.

anchors.label: Reynolds killed
anchors.animation_shows: Chronology event t28 (significance critical, old map label 7:20am): 'REYNOLDS KILLED ... at the eastern edge of Herbst Woods ... Doubleday assumes corps command'; units U-I and U-I-1-1 (Iron Brigade). Neighbours t25-27 show Reynolds reaching the seminary and the Iron Brigade double-quicking into Herbst Woods.

current_in_repo.note: evidence text cites a 10:40-10:50 dispute; none of that dispute is in the OR volume 27 corpus

anchors.reasoned_choice: Two reports of the First Corps, one written on 4 July by the division commander on the field (Wadsworth) and one by Doubleday in December, both say about 10:15; Buford (3:20 p.m. dispatch of the day) puts the start of the 'tremendous battle' at 9:30 and Cutler's brigade was in action from 10. Howard's 5 p.m. dispatch says 11:15, but Howard was not there and his formal report dates the arrival of Reynolds's aide with the news at about 11:30, so 11:15 is best read as the time the news reached him, an upper bound. Doubleday's report may rest on Wadsworth's, so the two are one family, not two independent witnesses. 10:15 is therefore a single-family estimate with a one-sided later bound; the window is 10:00 to 10:45.

conflicts.weight: preferred: eyewitness division commander, three days after
rejected as the time of death: second-hand, and Howard's own report puts the news at about 11:30

anchors.label: Lee's 'if practicable' order to Ewell
anchors.animation_shows: Chronology event t75 (critical, old label 11:15am): 'LEE'S DISCRETIONARY ORDER TO EWELL: take Cemetery Hill if practicable ... Ewell ... decides it is not practicable. Does not order the attack.'; unit C-II (Ewell's corps). t72 (Hancock rallies the Union on Cemetery Hill) precedes it, t90 follows. It is also the re-pointed Turning Points tick for 'Ewell's Discretion on Cemetery Hill' (was 175, provisional).

current_in_repo.note: 'after 5 p.m.' rests on a search summary that was never opened

anchors.reasoned_choice: No primary source gives a clock time for the order. What the sources fix: (1) it was sent while Lee 'witnessed the flight of the Federals through Gettysburg and up the hills beyond' (Taylor, who carried it, 1877), that flight began when Howard ordered the retreat at 4:10 (Doubleday says his corps retired at 3:45) and the columns reached Cemetery Hill at 4:30 (Howard); (2) Ewell received it 'on entering the town' (Ewell) when Johnson was reported close; Johnson's leading units reached the field between about 6:30 and sunset (Walker, Richardson, Latimer), which caps the order at about 18:30 on Ewell's own account; (3) Hancock's 5:25 p.m. dispatch finds 'the battle quiet' and no Confederate advance in progress. The probable window is therefore 16:15 to 17:30. 16:45 is a WORKING value inside it, not a finding. The 17:00 now on the anchor, and the 'after 5 p.m.' behind it, could not be traced to any source I could read. Trimble's 1898 account puts the same afternoon 1 to 1.5 hours too early and is rejected as a clock source.

anchors.label: XII Corps (and Johnson's division) arrive
anchors.animation_shows: Chronology event t90 (high, old label 12:30pm): 'XII Corps (Williams) arrives on Baltimore Pike and takes position on Culp's Hill. Greene's brigade on the right. Powers Hill reserve.'; unit U-XII only. Johnson's Confederate division is NOT in this event (it is the second fact row, R038/R039, of the anchor).

current_in_repo.note: 'a compromise between two ranges, not a measurement'

anchors.reasoned_choice: For the event the animation shows (the XII Corps in place on the Union right) the sources split: first infantry near the field about 4 p.m. (Crane); Slocum still 'moving' at 3:35; Geary in position on the left at 5 (his own figure); Hancock puts Slocum's arrival between 5 and 6; Ruger repositions about sunset; Howard and Meade say Slocum reached the cemetery about 7. I choose 17:30, the centre of Hancock's explicit 'between 5 and 6' (an A1 by the officer who handed command to Slocum) and consistent with Geary's 5:00; this is a reasoned choice among sources, not an average of the 4:00 and 7:00 readings, which I keep as the ends of the window. Johnson (the other half of the anchor) is a different, later event: his division arrived 'about sunset' / 'near dark' (Richardson, Funk), an hour before sunset at the earliest (Walker), and was in line only after dark (Early). CONTENT DEFECT for the data owner: Culp's Hill was occupied by Greene's brigade on 2 July at about 6 a.m. (Greene), not on the evening of 1 July; on 1 July the XII Corps stood on the Baltimore pike and the left, and Wadsworth held Culp's Hill that evening. The card text 'takes position on Culp's Hill' belongs to the morning of 2 July (tick 226-236).

anchors.label: Sickles advances III Corps to the Peach Orchard / Emmitsburg road
anchors.animation_shows: Chronology event t248 (critical, old label 6:50am): 'Sickles advances his entire III Corps to the Peach Orchard -- without orders ... exposed apex at the Orchard ... thin line stretching to Devil's Den'; unit U-III. Placement data at t248: U-III-1-1 (Ward) 'advanced to Devil's Den area', U-III-2-1 (Carr) 'on Emmitsburg Road'. t240 is the Berdan reconnaissance (12:00); t256 Longstreet's assault (16:00).

current_in_repo.note: midpoint of the range; vignette V-007 says 'around 3:00'

anchors.reasoned_choice: The advance was a sequence, so there is no single instant. Randolph dates Sickles's announcement between 1 and 2; Birney's division was on the new line firing by about 3:30; Hancock (1863) says the Corps 'advanced ... about 3 p. m.' and Meade (1863) found Sickles 'in the act of advancing' at about 3; Humphreys moved forward 'about 4' and Hancock's 1864 testimony and Wilcox say about 4 for the visible movement. The animation's tick shows the corps advancing as one act, ending with Ward at Devil's Den and Carr on the road, which is the 14:00-16:00 phase. I choose 15:00 because the two corps-level reports of the neighbours who watched it (Hancock, Meade) agree on it, and move the anchor 30 minutes later than the repo's midpoint. Birney's own two accounts differ by an hour for the preceding reconnaissance (12:00 in 1863, 11:00 in 1864), which shows the size of the clock noise. The Confederate side only says the line was in place by about 4 (Longstreet).

anchors.label: Chamberlain's 20th Maine bayonet charge
anchors.animation_shows: Chronology event t275 (critical, old label 9:05am): 'CHAMBERLAIN'S BAYONET CHARGE ... 15th Alabama broken and retreating. Nearly 400 Confederate prisoners'; units U-20ME, C-15AL. Placement data: t267 20th Maine refused flank, t268 first Confederate assault, t270 'Vincent mortally wounded nearby', t275 'Charging Line'; C-15AL 'Chaotic Retreat' at t275. t267 (Vincent arrives) is 16:30 and t280 (Peach Orchard collapses) 18:30 in the anchor table.
anchors.reasoned_choice: Chamberlain's own report (6 July) and Rice's agree that the brigade went into position about 4 p.m.; Chamberlain adds an hour of severe fighting before the final assault and Rice more than half an hour of 'desperate' struggle on the left before the charge. The Confederate reports put Hood's advance at 4:00 to 4:30 (Bryan, Bane), and Oates (1878) puts his regiment's break and rally 'just about sunset' (19:32). That gives a charge between roughly 5:15 (4:00 + the first assaults) and 7:00 (sunset); the Union sources, which time the start and describe the duration, put it in the first half. I keep 18:00 with the window 17:15-19:00. Chamberlain's report says the 'fall of Colonel Vincent' was told him 'at dusk', after the charge; this does not pin the charge to dusk because it is the second event in his sequence. The 5:10 and 5:30 readings in the repo's summaries are not in the OR text and could not be sourced; the 'after 7 p.m.' reading would put the charge at or after sunset, which Oates's 'sunset' for the already-broken regiment allows only at its limit and sits at the extreme edge of Oates's 'sunset' (19:32), so I weight it low.

anchors.reasoned_choice: Both sides agree to within the usual watch noise: Hays was ordered forward 'a little before 8' (his order, about 19:50), Early ordered the advance 'a little before dusk' (before 20:04), Godwin's regiment moved at sunset (19:32), Harris and Wainwright say 'about dusk', Howard says the attack began between 7 and 8 and lasted under an hour, Schurz heard the fire between 8 and 9, and Tate says the crest was reached when it was 'fully dark'. current_in_repo.note: Wikipedia's two articles disagree (about 2:00 vs around 3:00)

anchors.reasoned_choice: The Union reports all describe the infantry emerging from the woods after their own fire was stopped at 2:30 (Hunt, Howard): Hancock's arithmetic (1:00 plus 'an hour and forty-five minutes' = 2:45), Hunt 'about 3', Harrow 'nearly 3', Devereux 'just about 3'. The Confederate reports that name the order are Peyton for Pickett's division, 2:30, Jones for Pettigrew, 'about 2', and Davis for Heth's left, 3. A step-off at 2:30 to 2:45 with the line visible and advancing across the open ground by 2:45 to 3:00 fits all of them except Jones (earlier) and Davis (later). I choose 14:45: the Confederate order (2:30) plus the minutes needed to form the line, which meets Hancock's computed 2:45 and Hunt's 'about 3' for the same line seen in the open. The 'about 2:00' reading (Wikipedia citing Hess/Sears/Wert/Coddington) was not checked against those books and fits only Jones; Longstreet's 'About 2 p. m.' is the lines reported in order, not the step-off. Walking time to the wall (about a mile) from 14:45 gives about 15:15-15:30 at the wall, within the 15:10-15:45 of anchor t551.
